solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put up partner whose wife earns the money?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun it describes: the man whose wife is the breadwinner

parts.note: to put someone up is to house them
a husband is a marriage partner

explanation.surface: A man asks whether to accommodate a spouse while his wife brings home the wages.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of a man, read as 'one whose wife earns the money'; the question mark flags that it is a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who keeps the home while his wife is the breadwinner is the classic picture of this domestic role.

clue.text: Detective takes position in gap

parts.note: DI is short for Detective Inspector
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A detective plants himself in a breach, ready for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the space or interval between two things.

clue.text: Parish event held in cafeteria

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the word cafeteria, sitting within it

explanation.surface: A church fundraiser is staged in a canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A village or parish summer fair with stalls and games is the typical English example.

clue.text: One takes pictures secretly, in this

definitions.meaning: the legal phrase 'in ___' means in private, behind closed doors

explanation.definitionFit: It is the photographic device, and the Latin word for chamber in the phrase meaning held in private.

clue.text: Big cat almost on temple

indicators.note: almost the whole word: its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a panther is a big cat

explanation.surface: A large feline climbs onto a shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a famous temple to all the gods; the word means such a temple.

clue.text: Precipitation small, at the moment

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
now means at present

explanation.surface: A weather report: only light rainfall currently.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one kind of moisture falling from the sky, alongside rain, sleet and hail.

clue.text: Offer view over tree

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
a pine is a tree

explanation.surface: Someone gives an opinion about a tree, or a view across woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: To state one's opinion is the meaning; 'view' here is opinion, not scenery.

clue.text: Opposed to a way to secure advantage

indicators.note: the article and the street abbreviation together secure, or hold, the advantage inside them

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a gain is an advantage

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a method of getting ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' reads as part of the phrase 'a way to secure advantage', but it is the containment signal: the first two pieces hold the advantage word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: As a preposition it means in opposition to, as in voting against a motion.

clue.text: Terence goes round canteen drunk for anniversary

indicators.note: the name's letters go around the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: Terry is the usual short form of the name Terence

indicators.note: drunk suggests the word canteen reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: Terence staggers around the canteen after too much to drink at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: Terence must first become his familiar short name before anything happens; 'drunk' then shuffles the canteen letters, which sit inside that short name.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-hundredth anniversary is one particular kind of anniversary, so the answer is an example.

clue.text: It's different in the south-east — I told you so

indicators.note: the word for different goes inside the compass abbreviation

parts.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east
other means different

explanation.surface: A remark that life is not the same in the south-east of England, with a smug retort.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are triumphant, childish retorts after being proved right.

clue.text: Wrote about tall building

indicators.note: about suggests the letters of the word wrote turned round into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone composed something on the subject of a skyscraper.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall, narrow structure, like a castle keep or a modern office block.

clue.text: Passes fish, making gesture of greeting

parts.note: hands means passes, as in passing something over
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a fish, oddly, as a way of saying hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking another person's right hand is a common way to greet or agree.

clue.text: Secure armchair: always returned here?

definitions.note: a description of a constituency standing for the noun

parts.note: safe means secure
an armchair is a seat

explanation.surface: A comfortable chair you always come back to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' is the British electoral sense: an MP is returned when re-elected. A constituency where one party always wins is the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics, a constituency where the same party's candidate is reliably re-elected each time.

clue.text: Price paid: consider that is pounds short

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the pounds letter is taken away

parts.note: to feel is to consider or think
L is the abbreviation for pounds (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A shopper thinks the price was a few pounds too little.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge paid for a service, such as a professional's charge or an entry charge.

clue.text: Clueless, not having this soft egg I scrambled

definitions.note: the idiom 'not have the ___' means to have no idea at all; the definition fills the gap

indicators.note: scrambled, as with eggs, means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook who has no idea, never having made a soft egg, scrambled it instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a fill-in: someone clueless doesn't have 'the ___ idea'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'I haven't the faintest idea' has a twin with this word, meaning being completely ignorant.

clue.text: No time for fat girl

indicators.note: no time means the time letter is removed

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: Someone with no time to spare for an overweight young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, a common short form of Susan.

clue.text: Contended with horseman, say, several days

indicators.note: say signals the words are spoken, a sound-alike

parts.note: contended means fought, and a horseman is a knight: fought plus knight

explanation.surface: A jousting contest with a mounted warrior lasting for days.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a period of fourteen days, so a specific span of several days; common British usage.

clue.text: Cancel fine received by endless noisy party

indicators.note: the fine word is taken in by the shortened party word
the last letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a revel is a lively celebration
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Someone calls off a loud, never-ending celebration and is handed a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' is not a penalty but OK; 'endless' trims REVEL to REVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revoke a licence or order is to withdraw or annul it, i.e. to cancel it.

clue.text: Collect in a church service

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic Eucharist service

explanation.surface: A collection is taken during a Catholic service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' looks like the noun for a short prayer, which fits the church setting, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to gather or accumulate a quantity of things.

clue.text: Spots: a card contains any number

indicators.note: the card word holds the number letter inside

parts.note: an ace is a playing card
N stands for any number in algebra

explanation.surface: A playing card covered in any number of pips.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin condition of pimples, especially in teenagers.

clue.text: Dislike missing a translation

indicators.note: the word lacks the letter given next, which is dropped

parts.note: an aversion is a strong dislike

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes a missing translation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendering of a text in another language, as in the King James rendering of the Bible.

clue.text: Mechanical repetition of sacred text in religious lessons

indicators.note: the sacred text abbreviation goes inside the lessons abbreviation

parts.note: RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Scripture classes involve learning holy texts by heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by mechanical repetition is learning by heart without understanding.

clue.text: Country retreat, note

parts.note: a den is a private retreat or study
to mark is to note or observe; a mark is also a note made on a page

explanation.surface: A note about a rural hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scandinavian nation, so an example of a country.

clue.text: A stunner — stare wildly

indicators.note: wildly means the letters of stare are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone gazes wide-eyed at a very attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunner' suggests a beauty, but here it is a weapon that stuns.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an electric weapon that temporarily incapacitates people, i.e. a device for stunning.
